name: User Profiles
description:
User profiles summarise relevant characteristics of people or groups who interact with a product or service. Profiles may describe experience, behaviours, contexts, capabilities, constraints and goals without constructing the fictional character typically associated with a persona.

They can provide a concise way to communicate meaningful differences within a user population.
whenToUse: Use user profiles when research reveals important user characteristics that should inform design but a full persona format would add unnecessary narrative detail.
steps: Identify characteristics that materially influence the design.
Describe each profile using evidence-based characteristics.
Include relevant capabilities, contexts and constraints.
lookOutFor: Profiles can become stereotypes if based primarily on demographics or assumptions.
Do not treat categories as mutually exclusive unless evidence supports doing so.
Focus on differences that have consequences for design.

resources.citation: Hackos, J. T. & Redish, J. C. (1998). *User and Task Analysis for Interface Design*. Wiley.
